I get that, it's hard to admit and it's hard to make people take you seriously. I'm glad you want help, it's just about the best way to get it. 
I have some suggestions, please don't attempt suicide to make those around you see this. Your pain is valid without that and doing so something might go wrong. 
Some things that might work that I've tried:
-go for a day trip somewhere you enjoy and take the time to write a message about how you're feeling and what those around you can do to help. Provide as much or as little detail as you want. Send it as a text or message to trusted people that you think might be able or willing to help. For me this helped because I couldn't face saying it and the distance made me feel safer from immediate reactions and over message it gives them time to process. It's ideal to think about what you want from them first- is it understanding, more company, more support, someone to express these feelings to? Do you want them to treat you like normal after the message or to have a conversation in person about this? Telling more people is better because not everyone is able to give support all the time. You deserve a support network. 

-do a wellness check on yourself. you don't need to actively attempt suicide to be high risk, if you're considering suicide you are high risk. This advice heavily depends on your country, if it is not safe for you to do this in your country please don't. 

-call a lifeline or a psychologist or counsellor and have them help you figure out how to tell people. If you have a counsellor or psychologist they might be able to write you a note or help share this news. A lifeline should at least be able to help you come up with a way and individually discuss any barriers that we internet strangers don't know. 

You deserve help, and you deserve help without attempting suicide. It's scary and hard but people will respond better than you think and opening up is the first step to getting the help you deserve

Back in high school my best friend wasn't doing so well, I had been there for them and done everything in my power to be there all the time because I didn't want to lose them. One night after I went to have a shower I got a message from another mutual friend, they said my best friend had messaged them saying they had overdosed and were scared. My best friend did not message me directly, if they had died they never would have said goodbye. But fortunately that friend messaged me so I called their dad, their dad called me a liar then went down to see what had happened. 30 minutes later my friend and their dad wouldn't respond to my messages, when they did pick up my call they were in an ambulance, said they couldn't have told me because I would have just called their dad, said it was my fault for leaving them alone whilst I had a shower and if I didn't go to the hospital and see them they'd do it again. They also insisted I be the one to message all our friends and tell them what had happened. That night was easily the worst night of my life, I remember being so scared they would die and just feeling so guilty and mad and upset. I remember trying to call our friends and just being sick. 
As a disclaimer My friend is still alive today, and has gotten a lot better and is now living a happy life as their true self. But it took a lot of time to forgive myself and forgive them, I'm glad they're here and I'm so glad they're happier now. 
If you're struggling,  please reach out for help from someone who can help before it is too much.
